land.text: Bohemia, raised to a kingdom in 1198 (infobox)

successors.note: The same state under a new rank: 'Duke Ottokar I ensured his elevation by the German king Philip of Swabia in 1198' and the duchy 'was raised to a hereditary Kingdom of Bohemia' (Duchy page). fx-51: the duchy now runs to 1197 as an imperial state (the Empire is not a successor: the page has it 'an Imperial State of the Holy Roman Empire' from 1002), and the kingdom-of-bohemia dossier (found 1198, counterpart this slug) takes over.

capitals.name: Prague
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Bořivoj I moved seat to Prague Castle: 875'; the body text says about 880, and the Bořivoj page says the duke 'or (more probably) his son Spytihněv' moved to the Hradčany. The seat before the move is not on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Bořivoj I
rulers.note: 'His reign over the Duchy of Bohemia is believed to have started about the year 870'; the infobox gives c. 867 to c. 889. The Duchy page has c. 875-888/9.

rulers.name: Boleslaus I
rulers.note: 'from 935 until his death in 972'; the infobox gives 15 July 967/972 and Cosmas dates his death 967. Wenceslaus was murdered in 935 'or in 929, according to other sources'.

rulers.name: Boleslaus II
rulers.note: 'Duke of Bohemia from 972 until his death in 999' (7 February 999); the infobox gives July 967/972.

correction.text: the Bohemian basin, 'formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm', a Moravian vassal from about 872

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 870-889: Bohemia as the duchy of Bořivoj I. 'It was formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm' (infobox 'Duchy established: c. 870'). Cliopatria has no Bohemian row before 896 and draws the land as direct Great Moravian territory from 860; the Bořivoj page calls Bohemia 'subordinated to Great Moravia', so the Great Moravia dossier carries the vassal tint from 872 (its ledger).

correction.text: shape unchanged; it holds 895-899 (from the Bohemian dukes' oath to Arnulf in June 895)

keyframe_review.note: 45,639 km2 (bbox 12.12-16.06E, 48.59-51.11N): Bohemia without Moravia. It holds from June 895, not 896: 'The Bohemian dukes accepted Arnulf's suzerainty in June 895', and from 890 to 894 Svatopluk 'took over the rule of the Bohemian duchy himself' (Bořivoj page). The infobox gives no area, so no comparison was possible.
45,570 km2, the same Bohemian basin; no page records a border change in 900-910. the pages opened record no Hungarian campaign in Bohemia (Moravia was attacked in 900).
45,768 km2, the same basin. Bohemia is a vassal of the East Frankish and then German kings: 'Wenceslaus maintained his ducal authority by submitting to King Henry in 929' (page).
45,745 km2, the same basin; no page records a border change. Wenceslaus's submission to Henry I in 929 and his murder in 935 (or 929) leave the territory as it was.

45,108 km2, the same basin (west edge 12.20E against 12.12E: drawing noise). 'In 936 [Boleslaus] moved into Thuringia' and fought Otto I to 950 ('recognized Otto's suzerainty and promised to resume the payment of the tribute'); no land changed hands.

correction.text: Bohemia and the Silesian slice 'conquered' by Boleslaus I, without Moravia, which Bohemia 'received ... after the defeat of the Magyars' in 955

keyframe_review.note: 84,403 km2 (bbox to 19.04E, 51.05N): Bohemia, Moravia and a slice of Silesia. The page says Boleslaus I 'conquered the adjacent lands of Moravia and Silesia' on taking the throne in 935 (no year for the conquest) but that Bohemia 'received the lands of Moravia' only after the 955 Battle of Lechfeld. This shape therefore holds from 955 with Moravia, and 947-954 is Bohemia and the Silesian slice only.

correction.text: Bohemia with Moravia and the Silesian slice

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 955-959: the Cliopatria 947 shape unchanged, with Moravia. 'after the defeat of the Magyars [at Lechfeld, 955] received the lands of Moravia in recognition of his services' (Duchy of Bohemia); the Boleslaus I page: 'Boleslaus freed the Moravian lands from Magyar raids'.

128,568 km2 (bbox to 20.38E, 51.78N): adds Kraków and its region. The page: Boleslaus I 'expanded farther to Kraków in the east' and 'By occupying the city of Kraków, he controlled important trade routes' (Boleslaus I page), both undated. The Mieszko page: 'the Czech rule over Lesser Poland was only nominal' for many historians, and Bohemia 'supposedly extended up to the Bug River and Styr River'. The shape is the maximal reading; the eastern frontier is soft. The infobox gives no area.
127,027 km2, the same extent as 960 (1,500 km2 of drawing noise). Same soft eastern frontier; nominal rule over Lesser Poland (Mieszko page).

correction.text: Bohemia and Moravia without Silesia, which Poland took in the 990 conflict

keyframe_review.note: 81,126 km2: Cliopatria shrinks the duchy to the 947 outline (Bohemia, Moravia and a Silesian slice). The Mieszko page: the 990 war 'resulted in a war with Mieszko, who was supported by Empress Theophanu'; Silesia 'was taken over by Poland' as a result (annexation 'possibly ... around 985'), and Lesser Poland 'possibly' earlier than 990. The shape still holds a Silesian slice; the page gives Silesia to Poland, so it is removed.

correction.text: Bohemia and Moravia without Silesia, to the enfeoffment of Vladivoj in 1002

keyframe_review.note: 81,126 km2, the same outline as 990-999, corrected the same way. The duchy ends in 1002: Vladivoj was enfeoffed by Henry II 'and what had been a fully sovereign duchy became part of the Holy Roman Empire'; after Vladivoj died 'the next year' (1003) Bolesław the Brave 'invaded Bohemia and Moravia and ruled as Boleslaus IV'. [fx-51: the duchy does not end in 1002 as Cliopatria's row does; it runs on, as an imperial state, to 1197 (keyframes _1005, _1019 and _1182).]

correction.text: Bohemia alone, without Moravia and Silesia: the Poles 'were expelled from Bohemia with help from Henry II' (1004) but Moravia was 'temporarily ruled by' Bolesław I of Poland until it was re-acquired in 1019 or 1029

keyframe_review.note: Gap years (fx-51, life-span gap): Cliopatria has no Bohemian row from 1003 to 1201 and drew the land as the Empire's own, though the page keeps the duchy going as an imperial fief ('what had been a fully sovereign duchy became part of the Holy Roman Empire', 1002). The 1000 outline of 81,126 km2 is reused, cut to Bohemia while Moravia is Polish (page: 'the Polish duke Bolesław I the Brave invaded Bohemia and Moravia' in 1003; 'the Poles' expelled from Bohemia, then Duke Jaromír 'received the duchy in fief from the king'; Moravia 're-acquired ... in 1019 or 1029'). Confidence 1 for the exact edges: the page gives no border.

correction.text: Bohemia and Moravia without Silesia, the 1000 outline: Moravia was 're-acquired ... in 1019 or 1029' and 'thenceforth ... usually ruled by a younger son of the Bohemian duke/king'; the Silesian land Bretislaus took in 1039 is not drawn here (the Poland dossier's events carry it)

keyframe_review.note: Gap years 1019-1181 (fx-51): the 1000 outline reused. Pages opened give no border change for Bohemia proper to 1182. Silesia: the page has Bretislaus conquer 'part of Silesia including Breslau' (1039) and, 'the next year', Henry III force him 'to renounce all of his conquests except Moravia', while the Poland dossier's page has Casimir seize 'Bohemian-controlled Silesia' in 1050; the pages disagree on the year, so no Silesian gain or loss is added here and the Poland dossier's 1039 and 1050 events carry it. 1085: 'Henry gave Vratislaus a lifetime appointment as the first King of Bohemia'; 1158: 'Vladislaus was elected king of Bohemia on 11 January 1158': personal titles, not a change of state, so no rename is added.

correction.text: Bohemia without Moravia: 'In 1182, the Margraviate was created at the behest of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa' by merging the Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo appanage principalities, and the duchy, raised to a kingdom in 1198, is the Kingdom of Bohemia's predecessor

keyframe_review.note: Gap years 1182-1197 (fx-51): Moravia is the margraviate-of-moravia dossier's from 1182 (its found event names this dossier as counterpart). The Moravia page lists Conrad II Otto as margrave 'united with Bohemia 1189-1197' and says Moravia was 'variously a de facto independent state, and also subject to the Duchy, later the Kingdom of Bohemia'; that is a relation of rank, not a transfer of land, and is left to data/hierarchy.csv. 'Ottokar I (last duke, king to 1230)' is the infobox's 1197-98 duke.

region.text: the Bohemian basin, 'formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm'

ledger.note: c. 870: the Czech duchy of Bořivoj I arises inside the Moravian realm. 'It was formed around 870 by Czechs as part of the Great Moravian realm'; Bořivoj's reign 'is believed to have started about the year 870'. Moravian suzerainty from about 872 is in the Great Moravia dossier's ledger (vassal_start).

region.text: the Bohemian duchy, whose rule Svatopluk 'took over ... himself'

ledger.note: Winter 890: Svatopluk of Moravia takes over the Bohemian duchy. After Bořivoj died c. 889, 'King Svatopluk concluded an agreement with the East Frankish ruler Arnulf of Carinthia and took over the rule of the Bohemian duchy himself' (Svatopluk page: the meeting at Omuntesperch, winter 890). [Reviewer eu-15-a, 2026-10-25: source changed to the Svatopluk I page, which has 'during the winter of 890'; the Bořivoj page gives no 890]

region.text: the Bohemian duchy, freed from Svatopluk's successors

ledger.note: June 895: the Bohemian dukes swear fealty to Arnulf and leave the Moravian realm. 'The Bohemian dukes accepted Arnulf's suzerainty in June 895'; Duchy of Bohemia page: 'swore fealty to the East Frankish king Arnulf in 895'. Mojmír II failed to restore Moravian supremacy 'in the next two years'.

region.text: the Silesian slice: 'conquered the adjacent lands of Moravia and Silesia'

ledger.note: c. 947: Boleslaus I's conquests take in Silesia. 'Assuming the Bohemian throne in 935, Duke Boleslaus conquered the adjacent lands of Moravia and Silesia.' The page gives no year for the conquest; 947 is Cliopatria's. Piast Poland (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland starts 962) borders it on the north and east.

region.text: 'the lands of Moravia' received after Lechfeld

ledger.note: 955: after Lechfeld Boleslaus I receives Moravia. 'fought in the 955 Battle of Lechfeld and after the defeat of the Magyars received the lands of Moravia in recognition of his services.' The Boleslaus I page says he 'freed the Moravian lands from Magyar raids'. Neither page names a state that held Moravia 907-955; Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shape reaches 49.45N from 911, so some of it may be Hungarian-held. Bretislaus I 're-acquired the Moravian lands in 1019 or 1029' (page), after the Polish occupation.

region.text: 'expanded farther to Kraków in the east'

ledger.note: c. 960: Boleslaus I's reach extends to Kraków. 'By occupying the city of Kraków, he controlled important trade routes from Prague to Kiev and Lviv.' The page gives no year; 960 is Cliopatria's. The Mieszko page calls Czech rule over Lesser Poland 'only nominal'. Cliopatria's 44,000 km2 addition also reaches west Slovakia and northern Silesia, which no page names.

region.text: Silesia and Lesser Poland with Kraków, 'the lands of Silesia and Lesser Poland'

ledger.note: 990: Mieszko I of Poland takes Silesia and Lesser Poland from Bohemia. The 990 war 'resulted in a war with Mieszko, who was supported by Empress Theophanu'; Silesia 'was taken over by Poland'; annexation 'possibly took place around 985'; Lesser Poland 'Possibly, Mieszko took the region before 990'. Boleslaus II page: from about 990 'he sparked a long-lasting conflict with Poland around the lands of Silesia and Lesser Poland'. The year is the page's war year, the land's exact date is not.

region.text: Bohemia, where Bolesław I ruled as 'Boleslaus IV'

ledger.note: 1003: Bolesław I the Brave of Poland takes Bohemia. After Vladivoj's death 'the next year' (1003) 'the Polish duke Bolesław I the Brave invaded Bohemia and Moravia' and ruled as Boleslaus IV (Duchy page). Mirrors the Poland dossier's gain of Bohemia in 1003; the page gives no month.

1003: Moravia passes to Poland. The page has Bolesław invade 'Bohemia and Moravia' in 1003 and Bretislaus 're-acquire' the Moravian lands in 1019 or 1029; the Moravia page: 'Temporarily ruled by King Bolesław I Chrobry of Poland from 999 until 1019'. The region is the researcher's reading of 'Moravia'; the Poland dossier dates its gain 'c. 1003'.

region.text: Bohemia, from which the Poles were expelled

ledger.note: 1004: the Poles are expelled from Bohemia with Henry II's help and Duke Jaromír receives the duchy in fief from the king (Duchy page: 'after the Poles were expelled from Bohemia with help from Henry II'). Mirrors the Poland dossier's loss of Bohemia in 1004 (September, there).

1019: Bohemia re-acquires Moravia. The Duchy page: Bretislaus 're-acquired the Moravian lands in 1019 or 1029'; the Moravia page: 'Temporarily ruled by King Bolesław I Chrobry of Poland from 999 until 1019, Moravia was re-conquered by Duke Oldřich of Bohemia' (it names Oldřich, not Bretislaus). 1019 is the year both pages share; the Poland dossier ends its hold in 1018.

region.text: Moravia, the Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo appanages merged into the Margraviate

ledger.note: 1182: Moravia is made a margraviate of its own. The Moravia page: 'In 1182, the Margraviate was created at the behest of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa' by merging 'the three Přemyslid appanage principalities of Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo' and giving it to Conrad II. The page also has Moravia 'united with Bohemia 1189-1197' under Conrad II Otto and 'subject to the Duchy, later the Kingdom of Bohemia', so the loss is of the duchy's direct rule, not of its overlordship (hierarchy.csv).

region.text: Bohemia, the duchy raised to a kingdom in 1198

ledger.note: 1197: the last year of the duchy; in 1198 'Duke Ottokar I ensured his elevation by the German king Philip of Swabia' and the duchy 'was raised to a hereditary Kingdom of Bohemia' (Duchy page), which the kingdom-of-bohemia dossier (found 1198, counterpart this slug) draws. The 1002 dissolve into the Empire this event replaces was Cliopatria's row end (1002), not the end of the state: 'In 1002, Duke Vladivoj was enfeoffed with the Duchy of Bohemia from the hands of King Henry II of Germany' made it 'an Imperial State of the Holy Roman Empire', an overlord relation, not an end.

wars.name: Boleslaus I's war with Otto I
wars.outcome: Boleslaus stopped paying tribute, 'in 936 moved into Thuringia'; in 950 Otto I besieged a castle held by Boleslaus's son and Boleslaus 'recognized Otto's suzerainty and promised to resume the payment of the tribute'.
wars.note: The Boleslaus I page says the war 'reached its conclusion in 950' and dates its start to his accession in 935, giving no 936. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Battle of Lechfeld

zones.text: the lands of Moravia, received after the defeat of the Magyars

wars.outcome: Bohemian troops fought as Otto I's allies; 'after the defeat of the Magyars [Boleslaus] received the lands of Moravia in recognition of his services'.
wars.note: The Boleslaus I page puts it five years after the war with Otto and has Boleslaus 'free the Moravian lands from Magyar raids'.

wars.name: Bohemian-Polish conflict over Silesia and Lesser Poland
wars.outcome: Mieszko I took Silesia (annexation 'possibly ... around 985', 'taken over by Poland' after the 990 war) and Lesser Poland (possibly before 990); Bohemia's rule over Lesser Poland had been 'only nominal'. Boleslaus II: a 'long-lasting conflict' from about 990.
wars.note: The years are a span of the page's dates (985 annexation of Silesia, 990 war, 999 Boleslaus II's death); 'the conquest of lands around the lower Vistula' in 999 is Cosmas's report on the Mieszko page.

certainty.note: The Bohemian basin is bounded by mountains and the frontier is approximate throughout; the conquests east (Silesia, Kraków) are soft and, per the Mieszko page, partly nominal; no treaty line is on any page opened. 1003-1197 (fx-51): the 1000 outline reused; the pages opened give no border for Bohemia proper, and Moravia's edge follows the 1003-1019 Polish hold and the 1182 margraviate.

notes: Duchy of Bohemia, eu-15-a. Start 870 follows the infobox ('Duchy established: c. 870'); Cliopatria has no row before 896 because it draws Bohemia inside Great Moravia from 860. Dossier choice: Bohemia 870-889 is drawn here (new keyframe _870) and carried as a Moravian vassal by the Great Moravia ledger from 872; 890-894 Svatopluk rules it directly (Bohemia loss 890, gain June 895). Cliopatria years kept at confidence 1 where the pages are silent on a border move (947 Silesian slice, 960 Kraków). Conflict on Moravia: the Duchy page says Boleslaus I 'conquered' Moravia on taking the throne in 935 and also that Bohemia 'received the lands of Moravia' after Lechfeld in 955; the dossier follows the dated 955. The 990 shape still holds a Silesian slice; the Mieszko page gives Silesia to Poland, so it is removed by verdict. The Duchy of Bohemia continues to 1198 as an imperial duchy and then the Kingdom of Bohemia (Cliopatria row from 1202): 1003-1201 has no Cliopatria row and was outside this agent's page budget (see gaps). Rulers listed only where a page opened gives reign years (Bořivoj I, Boleslaus I, Boleslaus II); Spytihněv I, Vratislaus I, Wenceslaus and Boleslaus III have no dates on the pages opened. Bolesław I the Brave's invasion of Bohemia and Moravia in 1003 ('the next year' after Vladivoj's 1002 enfeoffment) and the expulsion of the Poles in 1004 with Henry II's help (Duchy of Bohemia page) fall after this dossier's last year; the Poland and Holy Roman Empire dossiers should carry them, and Moravia stayed Polish until Bretislaus I 're-acquired' it in 1019 or 1029. Prague bishopric founded 973 'through the joint efforts of Duke Boleslaus II and Emperor Otto I' (not a border). The Libice massacre of 28 September 995 is not a border event. Vassalage to the East Frankish and German kings (929 Wenceslaus's submission, 950 Otto's suzerainty, 895 Arnulf's) is the Kingdom of Germany / East Franks dossiers' to record as vassal events. Gazetteer: Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Lesser Poland are regions already in the gazetteer. FX-51 (2 Nov 2026, life-span gap): the dossier no longer ends in 1002. Cliopatria's Duchy row stops there and the Empire's shape drew Bohemia as its own land 1003-1197, but the Duchy page keeps one duchy from 870 to 'raised to a hereditary Kingdom of Bohemia' in 1198 (kingdom-of-bohemia found 1198, counterpart this slug; margraviate-of-moravia found 1182, counterpart this slug). The dissolve moved to 1197 (into kingdom-of-bohemia), new keyframes _1005 (Bohemia alone while Moravia is Polish), _1019 (Bohemia and Moravia) and _1182 (Bohemia without the margraviate), and mirror events for the Polish hold of 1003-1004/1019 and the margraviate of 1182. The Silesian episode of 1039-1050 is not added (the Duchy page and the Poland dossier's page differ on the year Bohemia gave it up); the Poland dossier's 1039 and 1050 events carry it. Overlord relations for data/hierarchy.csv: this duchy inside the Empire from 1002, the margraviate inside this duchy 1182-1197.
